messages:
jordan-peopleops: Quick question — new hire (Ana) is on OPT with a cap-gap EAD that expires 4/5. She accepted offer for a remote start 4/1. Her physical EAD renewal card (I-765 replacement) got lost in the mail and USCIS shows 'card mailed'. Can we onboard her 4/1 remotely? Payroll and benefits need guidance.

samina-peopleops: @jordan-peopleops thanks for flagging. Short answer: we can provisionally onboard for payroll eligibility if we have acceptable I-9 documentation per DHS guidance, but we need the remote I-9 exception checklist completed + manager attestation.

ravi-engineering: From a team POV we need her in on 4/1 for a sprint kick-off. Is there a way to make offer start conditional on paperwork arriving? We can do delayed access until cleared.

jordan-peopleops: Plan I proposed to the manager: start 4/1 with network access reduced (no prod keys) until docs verified. Curious about payroll — if we add her as a contractor/payroll pending docs, can we run retro pay once the EAD arrives?

visa-legal: Hi all — for cap-gap/EAD situations: USCIS policy allows employers to rely on reasonable documentation and the employee's attestation when card is pending. For remote I-9, we must follow the COVID-era remote verification policy fallback: a live video verification + scan of documents, and then the employee must present original docs in person within 3 business days of return to office, or per our internal remote-i9 policy if never returning. Also, we can't knowingly continue employment if the EAD ultimately denied.

samina-peopleops: Steps from People Ops side: 1) Have Ana sign the provisional onboarding agreement (we have a template). 2) Complete the remote I-9 checklist (screencap of video, photos of front/back of EAD + passport, signed attestation). 3) Submit a ticket to Payroll with 'provisional new hire - retro pay eligible' tag. Payroll will hold direct deposit setup until final docs but can run a provisional paycheck; retro pay is possible once documentation is verified.

onboarding-bot: Automated checklist: new-hire packet sent to ana@personal.email, remote-i9-form link https://redwood.internal/hr/remote-i9, provisional-onboard-agreement template attached. Deadline: 4/1 9am PT.

jordan-peopleops: What about benefits enrollment cutoff? She's FT. Open enrollment timeframe for new hires is 30 days from start. If we mark start as 4/1 provisional, benefits will be triggered. Will benefits be backdated if docs delayed?

visa-legal: Benefits eligibility is an employer policy area — we can make her benefits effective on the documented start date. If employment is later rescinded for authorization reasons, benefits will be reversed per policy and any premium reimbursements handled via payroll. People Ops should coordinate with Benefits admin to track effective date.

samina-peopleops: I'll loop in benefits admin and payroll after Ana completes the remote-i9 packet. Also will ask manager to sign the manager attestation (sprint access limitations).

ravi-engineering: OK — manager attestation received. We'll gate prod access. Any notes on I-9 secondary documentation if EAD never arrives?

visa-legal: If EAD denied, we must terminate employment. If EAD not received but USCIS case shows 'card mailed', maintain documentation and reasonable monitoring. If the card is lost in mail, the employee should file a non-receipt and we can ask for replacement receipt. Keep all correspondence in the immigration case folder.

jordan-peopleops: Thanks everyone — I'll send Ana the provisional agreement and remote-i9 link now. Will update this thread when Payroll confirms the retro-pay workflow and when benefits are looped in. :thumbsup:

onboarding-bot: Ticket created HR-4583 (provisional-onboard/Ana). Assigned: samina-peopleops, payroll-team.
